transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-07
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Nina Patel (Redwood CSM), Priya Raman (Stratus Head of ML), Eric Stone (Stratus CTO), Lena Ortiz (Product Ops), Samir Joshi (SRE), Jules (data analyst)

Summary: final closeout sync for the 6-week POC; go/no-go and next steps for pilot handoff / commercial proposal.

[00:00] Maya Chen: okay, thanks everyone for joining, we know it's a lot at the end of quarter so we'll keep to 45, quick agenda, results, tuning notes, open items and next steps.
[00:18] Priya Raman: thanks Maya, appreciate it. quick context — team has been running the pilot across catalog search rerank and chat assist, key success criteria were p95 latency under 400ms for short queries, throughput of ~250 qps at 300ms avg, and cost per 1k tokens to be below the threshold we talked about.
[00:35] Diego Alvarez: mm-hmm, and just to add we ran two configs in parallel last week, the quantized ggml variant and the fp16 optimized on Dedicated instance, so we have side-by-side results.
[00:50] Jules: small note, some of the numbers in the sheet are a bit off because of timezones, I adjusted but FYI.
[00:56] Maya Chen: great call-out. Diego, can you run through the headline numbers?
[01:05] Diego Alvarez: yeah, so headline — for the catalog rerank workload the Redwood runtime delivered p95 of ~320ms on the Dedicated-backed nodes with batching set to 16 and prefix KV cache enabled. Cost per 1k tokens for that workload averaged $1.80 using the quant profile on the cheaper nodes and $2.40 on fp16 config. For chat assist end-to-end we saw p95 closer to 420ms on long prompts, but for short-turns it was under 380ms. There were a few long-context cases where the KV cash — uh cache — didn't hit as expected and that pushed latency.
[01:43] Priya Raman: so the long-context issues, are those regressions vs their baseline model? we compared to the on-prem model we had before.
[01:52] Diego Alvarez: some regression in recall for prompts > 2k tokens; we tuned prompt chunking and increased KV TTL which helped but a small percent — maybe 4-6% — of queries still returned less relevant results. Might be from quantization in edge cases.
[02:10] Lena Ortiz: how visible is that to end users? our ops folks saw a spike in support tickets midday on Tuesday.
[02:18] Samir Joshi: yeah it correlated with the inventory sync window, we had a lot of unusual long descriptions.
[02:25] Diego Alvarez: right, that pattern lines up. We put in a fallback policy to route those long requests to fp16 nodes, but that doubles cost for those calls.
[02:35] Eric Stone: cost math is the thing. if we go Dedicated, what is the committed capacity we need and the expected unit economics? we don't want to overcommit.
[02:44] Maya Chen: totally. Nina, you had some numbers prepared?
[02:48] Nina Patel: yes, we modelled a few commit tiers — small, med, large. For the tier that matches Stratus' peak, the committed monthly price with the Dedicated pool brings unit cost to about $1.30 per 1k tokens equivalent, including autoscaling buffer. If you add automatic fallback to fp16 for long contexts, that bumps effective cost to around $1.55. If you elect for Redwood Private on your VPC, there's a platform fee and slightly higher op cost due to network and KMS integrations, so estimate ~+$0.20 per 1k tokens.
[03:26] Priya Raman: comparison to our baseline — we are at about $1.95 per 1k tokens today on our in-house setup, so those numbers look favorable. Are you including caching benefits in that math?
[03:40] Nina Patel: yes, the numbers assume our prefix/KV cache hit rates from the pilot (about 28% across workloads). If you can increase hit-rate by tuning prompts and TTL we'll see more savings.
[03:52] Priya Raman: ok good. Diego, how hard is it for our SREs to tune caching TTLs and batching? we want to own ops eventually.
[04:00] Diego Alvarez: we gave Samir and team the runbook; tuning takes a couple hours to iterate, mostly around traffic shaping and burst policies. We'll share the exact scripts.
[04:10] Samir Joshi: got it, I skimmed the runbook, a few commands failed on our sandbox because of an IP rule, I'll poke at that today.
[04:18] Maya Chen: action item capture — Diego will share configs, Samir will test, Nina will send pricing.
[04:25] [05:00] Diego Alvarez: on the quality front, Jules ran the evals — overall accuracy/precision for rerank improved by 7% over baseline when using the fp16 path, but the quantized path had a 2% drop on long-tail entity recall. We can mitigate with prompt engineering or partial-fp16 fallback.
[05:45] Jules: yeah the sample set is in the shared sheet, there's a tab called 'long-context-failures' with examples. some proper nouns were mangled in transcription but it's there.
[05:58] Priya Raman: are there any security blockers for us moving to Dedicated? we need SOC2 type II and audit logs and SSO integration.
[06:08] Nina Patel: Dedicated includes SOC2 controls; we'll provide the compliance pack and SOC2 attestation. For SSO we support SAML and SCIM for provisioning; for Private we can sit in your VPC and integrate KMS/HSM.
[06:26] Eric Stone: KMS integrations are important — can you do BYOK?
[06:30] Nina Patel: yes, BYOK via your KMS is supported in Private, and for Dedicated we offer key wrapping and managed KMS integration. We'll send the security techpack.
[06:40] Priya Raman: good. From a timeline perspective, what do you need from us to proceed to procurement?
[06:47] Maya Chen: sign-off on the success matrix and a rough committed capacity number; then Redwood will produce a term sheet and we fast-track a pilot-to-paid conversion.
[06:56] Priya Raman: I'm comfortable taking the success matrix to execs. A couple clarifying q's — first, how do you measure the success metrics in the report? is it just p95 latency and cost or do you include business KPIs like conversion lift?
[07:09] Diego Alvarez: we included both technical SLOs and the business KPI the pilot tracked — search conversion for the catalog rerank. In the report we have a before/after cohort analysis showing a 2.4% bump in conversion for the test bucket.
[07:22] Lena Ortiz: that 2.4% is pretty material for our revenue math. what confidence interval is that?
[07:28] Diego Alvarez: about 95% CI, sample size over the 6 weeks was decent, I can send the statistical appendix.
[07:35] Priya Raman: ok great. Anything left on the runbook/ops side?
[07:40] Samir Joshi: just the IP rule thing and a question on observability retention — we need logs for 12 months. can Redwood support longer retention?
[07:49] Nina Patel: yes, we have add-ons for extended observability retention; we'll include pricing. We'll also export token-level traces for the queries you choose.
[07:59] Eric Stone: on performance tuning one final question — is there a recommended config for mixed workloads (search + chat) to avoid double autoscale?
[08:08] Diego Alvarez: recommend splitting routes by SLA and model variant; use smart-routing so chat uses lower-latency pool and rerank uses throughput-optimized nodes. We have a sample routing policy.
[08:20] Priya Raman: sounds good. Any open technical risks we didn't cover?
[08:25] Diego Alvarez: the remaining risk is the small percent of long-context recall failures under quantized profile; mitigation paths are fallback to fp16, extra prompt engineering, or targeted reindexing of embeddings for search.
[08:40] Priya Raman: what's the estimated delta in monthly ops if we pick fallback approach?
[08:44] Nina Patel: as I said earlier, effective unit cost goes to ~$1.55 with fallback, versus $1.30 without; we can model exact numbers for your traffic.
[08:55] Maya Chen: checkpoint — do we have an initial sense from Stratus on whether you'll pick Dedicated vs Private?
[09:02] Eric Stone: leaning Dedicated given the economics and Redwood's observability, but we'll want to evaluate Private for data residency in EU later.
[09:12] Priya Raman: yes, EU residency is a season 2 ask, not blocking the go-live.
[09:18] Maya Chen: perfect. final recap of next steps: Maya send final pilot report and perf sheet; Diego share tuning configs and scripts; Nina send pricing and SOC2/compliance pack; Priya sign off success matrix and schedule exec wrap-up.
[09:35] Priya Raman: I'll aim to get sign-off by next Tuesday.
[09:40] Lena Ortiz: thanks everyone, can we also have a 15-min demo for execs to show the user flows?
[09:45] Maya Chen: yes, we'll coordinate that.
[09:48] Maya Chen: anything else? (brief crosstalk)
[09:52] Jules: small nit — one of the notebook exports had a column header mis-encoded, I'll re-upload.
[09:58] Maya Chen: thanks Jules. All right, we'll follow up in threads. Appreciate the partnership, everyone.

End.
